title: Ezekiel 42
paragraphs: ¹ Then he led me out to the outer court by way of the north and brought me to the rooms that were across from the courtyard and from the outer wall on the north side. ² The building to the north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide. ³ Facing the twenty-cubit inner court and the outer-court pavement, the galleries ran opposite each other at three levels. ⁴ In front of the rooms was a walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long, with their doorways on the north. ⁵ The upper rooms were narrower, because the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors.

⁶ These upper rooms had no pillars like the pillars in the courts, so they were smaller than the lower and middle rooms, going back from the ground level. ⁷ The outer wall ran parallel to the rooms toward the outer court for fifty cubits. ⁸ while the row of rooms facing the outer court was fifty cubits long, and those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long. ⁹ Below the lower rooms was an entrance on the east side as one approached them from the outer court. ¹⁰ Where the outer court wall began, there were rooms along its south side, facing the temple courtyard and the outer wall.

¹¹ There was a walkway in front of them like the walkway of the rooms on the north. Their length and width were the same, and their exits and arrangements were the same. The south rooms were entered the same way as the north rooms — ¹² from the east, at the front of the passage where the inner wall begins. ¹³ Then he said to me, "The north and south rooms facing the temple courtyard are the holy rooms where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will deposit the most holy offerings — the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings — for the place is holy. ¹⁴ Once the priests have entered, they shall not go out from the holy area into the outer court without first removing the garments in which they minister, for those garments are holy. They shall put on other clothes before approaching the areas open to the people." ¹⁵ When he had finished measuring the inside of the temple area, he led me out through the east gate and measured all around.

¹⁶ He measured the east side with the measuring rod — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁷ He measured the north side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁸ He measured the south side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ¹⁹ He turned and measured the west side — five hundred cubits by the measuring rod. ²⁰ He measured the wall on all four sides. It was five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, creating a separation between what was holy and what was common.
